concepts.learning_objective: Describe the planned streets, drains and fortified areas of Harappan cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Dholavira.
Explain why Harappan builders chose bricks or stone depending on what was locally available.
Describe the form and features of stupas such as those at Sanchi and Bharhut and how the Buddha was represented.
Explain how rock-cut caves such as Udayagiri-Khandagiri and Ellora were carved and used.
Explain how Harappan wells, Shringaverpur's reservoirs and other structures harvested and stored water.
Describe the engineering, artistic and social role of stepwells and temple tanks.
Identify the main elements of a classical temple such as the gopuram, mandapa, garbhagriha and shikhara or vimana.
Explain the temple as a representation of Purusha and worship as a journey from the outer to the inner world.
Compare regional temples such as Brihadishvara, Lingaraja, Dilwara and Bishnupur by builder and material.
Identify the main features of a mosque such as the prayer hall facing Mecca, domes, minarets and the mihrab.
Explain how Indo-Islamic architecture blended Islamic building traditions with Indian craftsmanship.
Explain why forts were located strategically and how they were planned and supplied.
Describe palaces such as those at Agra, Orchha and Mysuru and the styles they reflect.
Distinguish mausoleums from cenotaphs and explain why tombs belong mainly to faiths that bury the dead.
Describe the features of Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal and the cultures they blend.

topics.title: Traditional Houses, Churches and Colonial Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the central-courtyard design of havelis and Chettinadu houses and what they reveal about their owners.
Describe how churches in India, especially in Kerala, adopted local architectural traditions.
Identify Indo-Saracenic architecture as a colonial style blending Islamic, Hindu and Gothic elements.
